beats.text: If we split all the world's wealth equally, nine out of ten people would get richer.
Researchers added up what every adult owns, minus debts.
Ten people. Each coin is one percent of all wealth.
Today, the richest one holds seventy-five coins. The poorest five share just two.
Split equally, everyone gets ten. That's over a hundred thousand dollars each.
If your stack feels small, you're in the majority.

sources: World Inequality Lab (2025), World Inequality Report 2026 (Chancel, Piketty et al.) – global wealth 2025 (PPP): top 10 % own 75 %, top 1 % own 37 %, bottom 50 % own 2 %; a person in the bottom 50 % owns about $6,500, someone in the top 10 % around $1 million (pp. 38–39). Equal split per adult derived: $1M × 10 % / 75 % ≈ $133,000 (≈ $160,000 via the bottom-50 % figure) → 'over a hundred thousand dollars'. Deciles schematic: 0.4/0.4/0.4/0.4/0.4 · 6/6/6/5 · 75 coins.

Cross-check: UBS Global Wealth Report 2026 – wealth bands 2025: 58 million millionaires hold $250.6 trillion (48.4 %), 1.62 billion adults under $10,000 hold $3.2 trillion; ≈ $518 trillion over ≈ 3.85 billion adults ≈ $134,000 per adult (56 markets, >92 % of world wealth).
